statement_record.book: Given a monad (T, eta, mu) on C, construct the Kleisli category C_T — objects those of C, an arrow A_T → B_T being an arrow A → TB of C, identity eta_A, composite g_T ∘ f_T := mu_C ∘ T g_T ∘ f_T — verify it is a category, and construct an adjunction F ⊣ U with U : C_T → C such that T = U∘F, the unit is the given eta and mu = U epsilon_F.
statement_record.intree: Program Definition Kleisli : Category := {| obj := C; hom := fun x y => x ~> M y; id := ret; compose := fun x y z f g => join ∘ fmap[M] f ∘ g |};  Program Definition Kleisli_Adjunction : Kleisli_Free ⊣ Kleisli_Forget;  Theorem Kleisli_Monad_agrees : Kleisli_Forget ◯ Kleisli_Free ≈ M.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same. Objects, homs, identity and composition match Awodey's definition on the nose (his mu_C ∘ T g_T ∘ f_T is the in-tree join ∘ fmap[M] f ∘ g); the category laws are discharged from the monad laws as he asks; the adjunction is built and all three required agreements are proved — T = U∘F (Kleisli_Monad_agrees, with identity iso components), unit = eta (Kleisli_unit_agrees, by reflexivity) and mu = U epsilon_F (Kleisli_join_agrees).
